headline: Approved first reading of policies on conflicts of interest, nepotism, and committee concerns; approved expulsion with services for two students.
summary: The meeting covered field trips, a special education report, a multilingual report, NWEA scores, nutrition funding, a code of ethics procedure, and the superintendent evaluation. Members approved two field trips and first readings of five policies. They also approved expulsion with services for two students after closed sessions.
decisions: Approved field trip to Ecology School in Saco, Maine, 9-0.
Approved field trip to Saint Anselm and Southern New Hampshire University in Manchester, NH, 9-0.
Approved first reading of policy BCA-R, School Committee Concern Procedure, 7-2.
Approved first reading of policies BCB, BCC, BDE, and BDE-R, 9-0.
Approved expulsion with services for Student A, 9-0.
Approved expulsion with services for Student B, 9-0.

FIELD TRIPS 
Jake Langlais presented. 
VOTED: (1) Motion to approve the field trip request to attend Ecology School in Saco, Maine. Janet Beaudoin –

Jake Langlais presented. 
VOTED: (2) Motion to approve the field trip request to attend Saint Anselm and Southern New Hampshire 
University in Manchester, NH. Janet Beaudoin – Meghan Hird (9-0) 
 
SPECIAL EDUCATION  
 Kirsten Crafts and Charlotte Johnson recognized Sammy McClellan. Kirsten Crafts shared the 
 organizational chart, programs and CDS - Cohort 4. 
 
MULTILINGUAL BOARD REPORT 
 Lysa McLemore gave an overview of numbers, professional development, staffing, access update, and family 
 communications. We have 39 different home languages represented.  As a district we are 36% Multilingual. 
 We have 60 filled staff positions and 2 vacant positions.
MINUTES – LEWISTON SCHOOL COMMITTEE MEETING HELD OCTOBER 19, 2026 – PAGE 3 
 
NWEA SCORES AND GOALS DASHBOARD 
 Steve Maroon presented. Steve shared RIT Scores, national average measures, state average measures and 
 growth. 
 
NUTRITION  
 Superintendent Jake Langlais gave an update on Nutrition Funding.  
 
PROCEDURE 
Superintendent Jake Langlais reviewed the policy – Procedure for code of ethics violations. Procedure with 
steps was shared. Support was mixed in comments. Does not mean problems cannot be discussed informally. 
 
POLICIES 
Assistant Superintendent Karen Paquette presented. 
VOTED: (3) Motion to approve the 1ST read of the following policy:  
Elizabeth Eames – Lynnea Hawkins. (7-2) M. Hird, J. Beaudoin 
a.  BCA-R - School Committee Concern Procedure 
Luke Jensen proposed removing roles/seats 
 
VOTED: (4) Motion to approve the 1ST read of the following policies:  
Luke Jensen – Emily Levasseur. (9-0) 
b. BCB -School Committee Member Conflict of Interest  
c. BCC -Nepotism 
d. BDE -School Committee Standing Committees 
e. BDE-R -Standing Committee Operating Procedures 
 
SUPERINTENDENT EVALUATION 
 Superintendent Jake Langlais and Chairperson Phoenix McLaughlin reviewed the process of the 
 Superintendent Evaluation. We will get started. 
 
REPORT FROM SCHOOL COMMITTEE CHAIR 
 None. 
 
REPORT FROM SCHOOL SUPERINTENDENT 
Superintendent Jake Langlais reported the Say Something implementation plan is in progress. It will go live 
on November 1st or sooner.  We have made progress on the training model for our volunteer component. 
We are working on building a database and getting a list of kids that have signed the media release forms. 
There is a discussion about reducing, changing or cutting entirely the E-Rate funding at the Federal level. 
We have been working on an idea of creating a lottery to allow a minimum number of people per year to 
use a day before or after a break to travel. 
 
REPORT FROM CITY COUNCIL REP 
 The City Council is meeting tomorrow evening at 7:00 PM. Agenda items include the ordinance on mobile 
 home lot rents, an amendment to the trash ordinance, and other items.  
 
UPDATES FROM SCHOOL COMMITTEE SUBCOMMITTEES 
 Negotiations – CPE will start next week. 
 
SCHOOL COMMITTEE COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS 
 On Sunday there will be a vigil on remembering the events of October 25th at Simard-Payne Memorial Park at 
 6:00 PM. 
 
FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS 
 None.
